purpose_of_this_fixture: Tests gap detection on a weak discovery call at a residential pest control and lawn care company (about 60 technicians, two branches). Attending: a customer service lead and a dispatcher. The owner, Gary, is the real decision maker and is only mentioned. The consultant pitches before listening, offers fixes while the client is still describing pains, never works out a cost, accepts a vague why-now, pitches an unrequested customer self-service form that draws a polite hedge ('Oh. Huh. That sounds interesting.'), promises rough pricing, and ends with 'I'll send something over' and no date, time or owner. Expected behaviour: (1) Rubric: Partial for R1 to R9; Missing for R10, R11 and R12; nothing Met. R2 is Partial because no pain is excavated: P1 and P2 each have Stated and Concrete Met, but both clients defend their workaround ('the sheet's fine', 'the board works') and are cut off before saying why it cannot continue. R4 is Partial on a single hours figure (about two hours every morning) with no cost. (2) Record that hours figure as a cost input without inventing a wage, season length, weekly total or yearly bleed. (3) Verdict 'Nearly ready' by the section 2.4 rule, but the blueprint gate fails (R2 not Met) and pricing prep is held (R4, R7, R12 not Met). The plugin must not propose a blueprint, build or pricing. It produces a discovery prep with at most five gap questions, core criteria first, and a recap draft that proposes a specific time with Gary invited. (4) Product fit under v1 scope, which is Work Management plus CRM plus Service: Work Management is the build target for dispatch exceptions, lawn rounds and add-on requests, and monday Service is the build target for the intake the consultant kept pitching (re-treats, callbacks and complaints), because Service is in v1 at the same depth as CRM. The Service work must land on the account's NATIVE Service Tickets board, never a look-alike request board in Work Management and never the client's own 'service ticket', which is the visit record in their legacy software. The Service extras the consultant pitched hardest -- email-to-ticket intake, a customer self-service portal form and response targets that turn a complaint red -- are deferred beyond v1 and must not be named as deliverables. Do not choose monday CRM after Renata deflected that pitch. Service being in scope does not open the blueprint gate: still no build. (5) Treat pitched features that drew hedging as backlog, not needs. (6) Flag delivery issues: client talk share about 56% (under the 60% target), one consultant turn of about 245 words with no question (the opening product tour) and another of about 170 words (the routes-board pitch), fixes offered mid-description, and no commitment question. expected_questions_before_building is the full pool in priority order, not a list to ask in one meeting. account_context, expected_structures, accepted_behaviours and expected_leak_blocklist carry the account-shape, native-board, grader-tolerance and leak-check expectations.
transcript_format: Plain text with no timestamps and no call date. One speaker turn per paragraph in the form 'Name: text', turns separated by blank lines; the same speaker occasionally has two consecutive turns after a pause. Labels: Consultant, Renata, Travis (first names only; surnames are never stated). Stage notes in square brackets ([laughs], [crosstalk] twice, [radio chatter], [inaudible]); interrupted or cut-off speech ends with ' --'. ASCII only. About 3,950 words (about 3,730 spoken), roughly 28 to 30 minutes of conversation. Each location in this key is the line number in transcript.txt (L#) and the speaker.

expected_monday_products.why: monday Work Management: build target once the blueprint gate is met or the consultant overrides it. It covers the work that is not request intake: daily dispatch exceptions by technician (call-outs, trucks down, re-treats to slot in, rain-day pushes), lawn plans and rounds with a timeline view and dependencies for the rain pushes, the notify-list call before spraying, skips that quietly become cancels, and add-on requests technicians flag on tickets. These are ordinary boards, so the native-board rule (A5) does not apply to them, and no portfolio is expected (see expected_structures). It sits next to 'the system', which stays the record for customers, plans, routes and state application records unless Gary decides otherwise.

monday Service: also a build target, because Service is in v1 at the same depth as CRM. The intake the consultant pitched repeatedly is a real fit -- re-treat and callback calls that currently stall between the callback sheet and the whiteboard, and complaints arriving from the phones, the office inbox, the website, online reviews and the owner's cell. These become items on the account's NATIVE Service Tickets board (A5), never a look-alike request board built in Work Management. Two hard limits. First, the deferred extras: the customer self-service portal form, email-to-ticket channels and SLA or response-target setup are out of v1, which strips out most of what the consultant actually demonstrated in words ('You could put a form right on your website', 'So all of that, the email, the phone, the website, it all lands in one place as tickets.', 'so if a complaint hasn't been touched by end of day it goes red'); requests still get in by manual entry or a plain monday form, and ageing is a status and a view rather than an SLA policy. Second, the vocabulary clash: Renata corrected the consultant that 'a service ticket for us is the actual visit. That's in the system.', so native Tickets items are their call-ins, not their visits. Nothing is built yet: the blueprint gate is shut.

traps: 'Callback' means different things: Renata uses it for any customer call-in that needs follow-up (re-treat, billing, wants a call), Travis for a truck going back out. Ask before naming a board, item type or status after it.
'The board' is the physical dispatch whiteboard, not a monday board.

'Service ticket' is a scheduled visit in the system, not a customer request. Renata corrected the consultant's 'that call becomes a ticket'. This collides with monday Service, whose native items are called tickets: their call-ins are the native Tickets items, their visits are not. Do not rename the native Tickets board to their meaning, do not map visit records onto it, and expect to need a different word for one of the two in anything client-facing.
'Leads' is ambiguous: add-on sales requests from tech notes (Renata) versus, probably, lead technicians ('My leads', Travis).

Service is in v1, so the intake the consultant pitched is genuinely in scope -- but it must go on the account's native Service Tickets board, not a look-alike. The tempting wrong move is a Work Management board called Tickets, Requests or Callbacks, built because today's intake lives on a Google Sheet. See expected_structures.lookalike_traps. In-scope does not mean build: the blueprint gate is still shut, so Service appears as the intended target, not as created objects.
Do not choose monday CRM. The consultant pitched a sales pipeline for add-ons and Renata deflected ('That's more Gary's side'). Add-on requests fit a simple Work Management board.

Only one hours figure exists (Travis, about two hours every morning, Saturdays too in season). No wage, hours per week, weeks in season or other roles' time was given. A weekly figure such as 10 to 12 hours would be [inferred]; do not compute a bleed from outside averages; ask.
Re-treat volume 'Fifteen, twenty a week, maybe?' is an unconfirmed range for the main branch only, and 'Summer's like double' is loose. Keep it as a range.

Why now is vague: 'it's kind of gotten worse, I don't know' names no change or date. The spring bad reviews and the North branch opening are possible triggers the client never connected to timing. Ask rather than assume.

The owner, Gary, is the likely approver but was not on the call. Lorna (North branch) and Kelsey (owner's daughter, built the callback sheet, may have used monday before) are possible stakeholders with unknown roles.
Whether North is in scope is open ('I don't know if it's going to North'), yet the consultant already suggested copying the setup to North.

'The system' stays according to Renata, unconfirmed with Gary. Its product name, data, export or API options and link to QuickBooks are unknown, and state application records must stay there.
